spec_markdown:
## Claim

The vulnerable snapshot is open to literal parent traversal, and the patched snapshot is an incomplete fix that blocks literal `..` but decodes percent escapes afterwards.

## Intended behavior

A clean relative name such as `data/greeting.txt` returns the UTF-8 text stored under `root`.

## Rejection behavior

Both `../secret.txt` and `%2e%2e/secret.txt` must be rejected. The same proof test must fail on both approved refs, so the expected verdict is REFUTED with reason PATCHED_STILL_LEAKS.

## Entry point

`pkg.codec.decode(name: str, root: str) -> str`

## Benign example

BENIGN: `decode("data/greeting.txt", root)` returns `hello from the fixture\n` when `root/data/greeting.txt` contains that text.

## Detector

Request the grader-provided `detector` fixture. Try both payloads, collect any payload that returns the secret content, and call `detector.check(bool(leaked), detail="...")`. Assert that no payload leaked. Do not read or hardcode a canary path.
